Sql.metaTitle: SQL & MySQL for engineers who ship
Sql.metaDescription: An opinionated, chapter-based course on the SQL and MySQL you'll actually write at work — from SELECT to replication, indexes to JSON.
Sql.intro: {chapters} chapters, {lessons} lessons. Real schemas, portable SQL first, then a deep dive into the MySQL features you'll actually use in production. The exact mental model I use when someone hands me a slow query at 4 PM on a Friday — no academic fluff.
Sql.demoClosing: By the end of this course, queries like this will feel obvious.

learn.mentalModel_body: Why SQL is about sets, and the seven-step execution order behind every query.
learn.joins_body: INNER vs LEFT vs FULL, EXISTS vs IN, and recursive CTEs — the four ways to combine row-sets.
learn.agg_body: GROUP BY, HAVING, conditional aggregates, ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG/LEAD, running totals.
learn.schema_body: Data types, constraints, normalization, and the indexes that earn their keep.
learn.tx_body: ACID, the four anomalies, REPEATABLE READ vs READ COMMITTED, deadlocks, SELECT FOR UPDATE.
learn.index_body: B+ trees, the buffer pool, covering indexes, and reading query plans without flinching.
learn.prog_body: Views, stored procedures, triggers, scheduled events — when they earn their place, and when they don't.
learn.ops_body: Users and privileges, mysqldump and XtraBackup, point-in-time recovery, replication, failover.
learn.modern_body: JSON columns with indexed paths, FULLTEXT search, generated columns, multi-valued indexes.

About.metaDescription: Naufal is a senior frontend Developer with a decade of experience leading design systems and building durable interfaces.
About.intro: I've spent the last ten years building interfaces that survive their own success — design systems that scale past their authors, apps that stay fast as the team grows, and codebases the next engineer can read without an introduction.
About.shortVersionP1: Senior frontend engineer based in Jakarta. I work at the intersection of design and engineering, with a strong bias toward the boring fundamentals: semantic HTML, accessible patterns, honest performance budgets, and APIs that age well.
About.shortVersionP2: I've led design systems at three companies, mentored more than sixty engineers, and shipped enough product to know which decisions matter and which are aesthetic preferences in disguise.
About.principlesTitle: What I care about, in four sentences.

principles.durability_body: The best frontend code is the code that's still readable in 2030.
principles.a11y_body: Not a compliance checkbox bolted on at the end.
principles.perf_body: Numbers in a Lighthouse report are downstream of architectural decisions.
principles.design_body: The earlier the meet, the cheaper the outcome.

experience.lumen_summary: Lead the design system and platform UI guild. Cut TTI 38% across the flagship app and shepherded the migration to React Server Components.
experience.northwind_summary: Owned the component library used by 80+ Developer. Wrote the accessibility playbook still in use today.
experience.halyard_summary: Shipped the first dashboard rewrite from Backbone to React. Stayed long enough to clean up after my own tech debt.

About.toolboxText: The list shifts, but the philosophy doesn't: pick boring tools with strong communities, then commit.
About.contactText: I'm selective about new work but always happy to talk shop.
